headnotes.text: A vessel is an oceanographic research vessel under the Oceanographic Research Vessels Act only if the Coast Guard finds it to be one; regulations in force before the 1981 designation rule already required such a finding. An operator that never obtained the designation cannot invoke the Act to deny an employee seaman status.

headnotes.text: A seaman does not lose that status because his employer temporarily assigns him to shore duties. Whether status continues is a fact question turning on the assignment's duration, its relation to the employer's business and seagoing work, and whether the employee could refuse it; a brief shore assignment preparatory to vessel work preserved seaman status.
